items.title: Descending purity along an inverse limit of affine schemes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma descends a finite presentation morphism together with a finitely presented module that is pure along a fibre and flat over the base at every point of that fibre: after possibly moving along the directed system there is a stage carrying a morphism and a module with the same properties whose base change is the given pair (statement lines 5377-5392, tag 05MA). The proof is a real limit argument: it descends the flat locus and its quasi-compact piece, builds an affine etale neighbourhood over a stage on which the module has projective global sections, rewrites purity as an inclusion of the relative associated primes, uses constructibility and base change compatibility of that inclusion so that it can be tested at a finite stage through the colimit description of the local ring at the limit, and then applies the purity criterion over that stage. The constructibility step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
